---
number: 99
title: M2.5 Part 3: Specifications, parts and verification as one layer
milestone: M2.5
labels:
  - Epic
---

Every function a contract computes is written twice (as cases in `FirstParts` and `ArithmeticParts`, and again in `Specifications` found by name), running a network exhaustively and checking it is written three times, counterexamples are strings, and the part records live in a file of hand-built fixtures that imports `Modules`; specs, CEGIS and a verifier pipeline all build on this.
We want one definition per function from which cases are made, a `Parts` home for the part records and library, and one verifier with typed verdicts and structured counterexamples.

Its responsibilities are:
* Specifications as the source of contract cases, latencies and port layouts
* Part records, the part library and the hand-built fixtures each in their own place, with the cycles through them broken
* One verifier and one definition of solved, with counterexamples as inputs a search can take

The contracts' cases should come out identical to today's, because existing parts and saved runs were verified against them.

Order: specifications; parts; verifier.

Done when: no function is defined twice, the verifier returns typed verdicts used by `evolve-parts`, `verify`, promotion and fitness, and the golden runs pass unchanged.

Read first: RESEARCH.md "Proving contracts", "Spec to verified circuit"
